newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds reversed the losses of the previous day to finish higher amid talk of large scale switching between guilder state loans and German bunds.
The Dutch currency also appreciated against the mark in an unusually robust show of strength, a move some attributed to speculation of a rise in Dutch short term interest rates.
A dealer said a large buyer was rumoured to be switching into guilder paper, although spreads to Germany actually widened. "It could be a large hedge fund," he said.
But another trader reported switching the other way in the 10-year sector.
"We experienced some foreign retail selling (of Dutch bonds) and pressure on shorter maturities. There's some closing of positions because of month end," he said.
Another dealer, citing short covering in the 2000 and 2001 maturities, said: "Some parts of the curve, especially the mid-part, saw some big buying."
Guilder loans took little notice of data showing a slowing U.S. economy but figures on Friday, including October jobs and NAPM, could make for volatile trading tomorrow, dealers said.
